subject: Incident follow-up: decoding KV cache inconsistency, timeline & mitigations
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@prioritypay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: Incident follow-up: decoding KV cache inconsistency, timeline & mitigations

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time on the call earlier. Attached is a concise RCA and evidence bundle; below is a short, customer-facing summary plus our concrete action milestones.

Executive summary (short):
- Root cause: an interaction between a new background compaction optimization and our KV cache eviction threshold produced a race that evicted active shards for long-lived sessions. This caused inconsistent prefix state to be served for ~0.7% of requests over a 27-minute window.
- Impact: elevated token latency and incorrect continuations for a subset of long-lived streaming sessions for PriorityPay between 2026-08-29T16:03:00Z and 2026-08-29T16:30:00Z.
- Business risk: incorrect outputs for those sessions (no data exfiltration).

What happened (timeline, high level):
1) 16:00 UTC — we rolled an optimization to background compaction that reduced memory pressure by aggressively re-sharding in certain autoscale buckets.
2) 16:03 UTC — under a small spike in concurrent long-lived sessions, the eviction threshold was hit for two KV shards; an eviction and immediate re-allocation sequence created a transient state where replicas served stale prefix keys.
3) 16:03–16:30 UTC — affected requests intermittently received inconsistent context leading to truncated or duplicated tokens.
4) 16:31 UTC — on-call alerted via synthetic monitors (latency + content regression).
5) 16:45 UTC — we rolled back the compaction change, deployed a hotfix that pauses aggressive re-sharding during active sessions, and began a reconciliation job for affected sessions.

Mitigations performed (already completed):
- Immediate rollback of the compaction change (16:45 UTC).
- Hotfix to block re-sharding during active sessions (deployed 16:52 UTC).
- Reconciliation job to compare prefix snapshots with persisted logs and repair 100% of impacted sessions (started 16:55 UTC).

Planned actions and owners (milestones):
- Short-term: integrity scan across all PriorityPay session namespaces — owner: Dylan Brooks — ETA: 2026-08-30 04:00 UTC.
- Medium-term: change eviction thresholds and add adaptive backoff to compaction — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: 2026-09-07.
- Long-term: add end-to-end session consistency checks and pre-deployment synthetic coverage for re-sharding changes — owner: Camila Reyes (program lead) — ETA: 2026-10-01.

Customer-visible items included in attachment: a 3-page PDF RCA (rca_20260829.pdf) and a log bundle with annotated excerpts (kvcache-log-bundle-20260829.tar.gz).

Next steps we propose:
- We will run the integrity scan and share a pass/fail summary within 12 hours.
- We propose a 30-minute technical readout tomorrow to walk through the artifacts and the verification plan. Proposed window: 2026-08-30 14:00–14:30 UTC.

If you want us to include any specific session IDs or additional logs for PriorityPay before the readout, tell us which ones and we’ll prioritize.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact and are treating this as a Sev-1.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Reliability PM, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachments: rca_20260829.pdf (PDF), kvcache-log-bundle-20260829.tar.gz (log bundle)
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@prioritypay.com>

Cc: ops@prioritypay.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 18:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: decoding KV cache inconsistency, timeline & mitigations

Camila —

Thanks for the clear summary and quick actions. A couple of quick questions:
1) Can you confirm there was no customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access during the window?
2) We run several long-lived streaming sessions across two regions — will the reconciliation job and integrity scan cover both regions and full session history?
3) We may ask for a credit for the affected window — what is Redwood’s standard approach here?

We can take the readout tomorrow at 14:00 UTC; include any security/compliance folks from your side.

Best,
Elena Torres
VP, Operations — PriorityPay
elena.torres@prioritypay.com

Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: decoding KV cache inconsistency, timeline & mitigations

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the quick reply and the questions. Answers below:

Q1 — data exfiltration: confirmed no evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized access. The issue is a state/consistency problem inside our serving layer; all access logs show requests remained authenticated and routed correctly. We’ve engaged our security team and will include the formal statement in the compliance package.

Q2 — regions & coverage: the reconciliation job is running across all PriorityPay namespaces in both regions where you run long-lived sessions; it reads persisted write-ahead logs and compares them to in-memory snapshots before applying repairs. We start with the session window 2026-08-29T15:45:00Z through 2026-08-29T16:45:00Z (buffered) and will expand if we find additional anomalies. Expected completion for the prioritized window: 2026-08-30 04:00 UTC (owner: Dylan Brooks). We will provide a CSV listing repaired session IDs and a checksum summary for verification.

Q3 — credits: we handle credits on a case-by-case basis for production-impact incidents. I’ve looped in Hannah (CS lead) to start the internal review; we will propose a credit calculation by EOD tomorrow after the integrity scan completes.

Security/compliance folks: Hannah will join the readout and will prepare the incident evidence package (SOC2-oriented items + access logs).

Readout logistics: confirmed — 2026-08-30 14:00 UTC. Link to readout materials and live artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/prioritypay-rca-20260829. Jira ticket for tracking: JIRA-3482.

Action owner snapshot (short):
- Dylan Brooks — integrity scan and repaired session report — due 2026-08-30 04:00 UTC.
- Marissa Cole — eviction & compaction tuning PR + test plan — due 2026-09-07.
- Hannah Schmitt — credits proposal and compliance package — due 2026-08-30 EOD.
- Camila Reyes — overall program lead, customer communications, and readout — ongoing.

If helpful I can include the exact list of session IDs we will scan before the readout.

Regards,
Camila
